This year can be said to be the first year of super apps. OpenAI recently launched its own super app and admitted that the program was "a bit chaotic." Microsoft CEO has also confirmed that a super app belonging to Copilot will soon be launched.

Microsoft Copilot "Super App" will integrate Cowork, chat, coding and other functions

Microsoft is developing an AI "super app" that combines Copilot chat, coding, and intelligent agent functions. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said on Wednesday's earnings call that the app will launch this year, covering "both consumer and commercial experiences." Nadella said: "Copilot is rapidly evolving from chat functionality to Cowork, and then to Autopilots. This quarter we are integrating these Copilot experiences—including coding functions—into the same super app... This is a significant development, and I look forward to sharing more details later."

OpenAI's process of launching its own "super app" can be described as a mess. But clearly it has not deterred other companies from adopting the super app approach.

Perhaps Microsoft can better build a multi-functional integrated app and avoid repeating OpenAI's mistakes.

That said, CEO Satya Nadella recently also stated that the company is gradually transitioning from apps to focusing on intelligent agents. The AI era is still in its infancy, and the trends and best practices for building AI-centric interfaces are constantly evolving.

As for Apple, so far there is no sign that it is moving toward the super app direction, instead continuing to launch various independent and specialized apps. Whether this strategy will change in the future is worth waiting to see.

What do you think about this recent wave of "super apps"? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comment section.
